utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Smith, you were examining Mr. Lojo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Smith: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lojo.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last Thursday I asked you the question, when you arrived in the KP Dom on the 19th of April, who appeared to be in charge. I said, "Was it a civilian or military authority?" You answered: "At that time people were just being brought in in numbers." The intensive groups which you'd previously described as well-trained paramilitary groups from Serbia, and to some extent joined by locals, were the ones who brought people in; and after only about a month, the guard service had been established and internal relations had begun to be organised. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the 19th of April, those first few days when you arrived at the KP Dom, who were the guards inside the KP Dom? Were they the same as the paramilitary groups that were bringing the Muslim detainees in, or were they a different group?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those early days when I was brought to the KP Dom, I think that at that time the guard service had not been put in place yet, and we found there some -- to begin with I said that one could often see so-called guardsmen, but they were members of paramilitary units who kept bringing in new prisoners all the time. And around the KP Dom, around the penitentiary, which also has a very tall -- high wall, one could see there some guards, and some of them even had dogs. But I do not think that right at the beginning they were those same guards who later on regularly performed their work duty. I cannot say definitely when it was that regular guards came, but it was at an early stage; that I am sure of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, you've stated that the guard service had been established within about a month or shortly after a month, and internal relations were organised.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is about it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did the -- the paramilitary troops, when did they leave?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left shortly after we came. I think they were there for about a month. I cannot fix the date because I simply was not in a position to follow their movements all the time. But be that as it may, they left about a month after I was brought to the KP Dom, they just disappeared. Or perhaps it could have been as much as two months, but I don't think they were there longer than two months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the internal relations within the KP Dom had been organised, who were the guards? Were they local people from the Foca municipality? Were they from outside? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the guards were organised, those were only those men who did the same job before in the KP Dom. There could have been a new person here and there, simply to replenish it to the strength and organise proper the guard shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know these guards as being people who worked at the KP Dom before the war broke out, or did you learn that afterwards?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know them because I never worked in the penitentiary. But there were -- amongst us there were also guards of Muslim origin who used to work for the penitentiary before the war, and one could see from the way they behaved that they knew those guards very well, I mean their fellow guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did these guards wear?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had uniforms and I think that those were camouflage uniforms, by and large. In the beginning they looked like military camouflage uniforms rather than the police ones. The police camouflage uniforms which were of blue/grey colours, they appeared later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the colour of the uniforms that the guards wore, what was that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were many-coloured, but I should say grey/green combinations in a regular pattern.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the guards' supervisor was, their immediate supervisor?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume it was a person whom we later on came to know very well and who was the guards' commander, and his name was Mitar Rasevic. He was the commander of the guards, the chief of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd just ask that P18 be placed on the ELMO. If the usher could do that, please. Prosecution Exhibit -- sorry, Prosecution Exhibit 88; it's a sketch of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, do you know whether Mr. Rasevic had an office at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, I really don't. All I know is he was somewhere here in the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone. We could not hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you did not hear. I really do not know where his office was exactly, but I guess it was in this part of the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you place the pointer on that part of the building again? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was in part 1 or part 2, but my guess is that it was somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicated buildings 1 and 2 on P88.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, about a month after you arrived at the KP Dom, did you know who was in charge of the prison, of KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know it at that time. At that time, I didn't know who Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was at the head of the penitentiary. "At that time" is a rather vague term, but I should say that until at least mid-May I was not aware of who was the warden of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after mid-May did you become aware of who was the warden at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, I did learn that Mr. Krnojelac had become the warden of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is Mr. Krnojelac's first name?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Krnojelac from before the war?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, even though not closely. I knew him because he was my teacher at school. And I knew some other teachers -- I knew them better than him -- who were his fellow teachers. Some of these teachers were my next-door neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of what he taught at school?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, maths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look around the courtroom today. Do you see Mr. Krnojelac in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please indicate Mr. Krnojelac to the Court. Can you point? Can you point with your finger?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac is over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That does not help very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, Your Honour. Just for certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But it still doesn't help to have recorded who it is he's pointing to. He should be able to say whether he is standing or seated or whatever the position is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, could you describe where Mr. Krnojelac is in the courtroom, who he's sitting next to, and what they are wearing?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac sits on my left next to the window, if that is a window. No. That is a booth. So next to the booths, between two policemen. He is wearing glasses and a headset. He has a black suit and a white shirt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that records that he is pointing to the accused. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any meetings with Mr. Krnojelac at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Mr. Krnojelac twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the first meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once it was at my and my brother's request when we asked to speak to him and announced our visit through the guard service because we wanted to talk to the warden, Krnojelac. At that time, we discussed or, rather, we tried to discuss if it will be possible for me and my brother to leave the prison somehow and to go through Montenegro to Macedonia because that's where our families were waiting. My family had been taken there -- had been taken there, and she was alone with four children, the eldest one being 15. My brother's wife was also there, whereas his children were in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We met here in a part of structure 3, building 3. No, no, no. No, not 3, 2. Here on the ground floor there is an office which is envisaged for those visiting prisoners, here, somewhere in this part but on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicates building number 2, on the ground floor, on Exhibit P88.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this meeting was held? Do you know what month?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that happened, I think, sometime in mid-June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I cannot be sure about the date, but as far as I can remember, it was about then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you request to speak to Mr. Krnojelac? Who did you ask to be able to meet with him?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to meet him we had to ask guards for that, and write our names on a piece of paper and then give it to the guard who then gave it to the warden or somebody in the administration and then we waited to be called in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you specifically ask to see Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because we thought that Mr. Krnojelac was an objective man, a realist, that he would understand the situation we were in. My brother is also a teacher, a lecturer, and I even think that Krnojelac was his student. I'm not absolutely sure about this, of course, but I think he was. However, the chief reason was, of course, the precarious situation in that camp. And we knew things that were going on. The situation was very hard, and we thought we should try, if it were possible, to get on to some exchange as quickly as possible. We knew that there were some deportations for people. And because we did not want to take part in the war, we simply wanted to get to our families as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did a guard escort you to the place where Mr. Krnojelac was or did you go there of your own accord?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He escorted us. We could not go there alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was in the room with this meeting with Mr. Krnojelac? You mentioned your brother and yourself. Was there anyone else with you during that meeting?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: An individual who at that time often supervised visitors, but he perhaps entered only once in the beginning, but Mr. Krnojelac told him to let us be, to have our discussion without him interrupting us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this person? Was he a guard or was he some other -- did he have some other role at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that person very well because he was there throughout our imprisonment. His surname is Matovic -- I don't think I mentioned his name in my statement -- and I believe he was in charge of some security matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Mr. Krnojelac told this person to let you be and to stop interrupting, what did this person do? Did he stay or leave?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left and closed the door. The door was shut after he left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Krnojelac's response to your request to your release from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he was slightly nervous when he said, "Just leave us alone. Don't interrupt." If I may add to my earlier statement why we went there. One of the reasons why we asked to be received was to express our condolences to Mr. Krnojelac because we had learned that his son had been severely wounded. So that was one of the reasons for our asking to see him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honours, but I'm not quite sure that the transcript or, rather, what it says in the transcript, I'm not sure that the witness answered the Prosecutor's question, because in line 20, it says that Krnojelac -- no. Excuse me. "What did Krnojelac answer?" That is the question of the Prosecutor. That is line 20. And in 22 is that he was slightly nervous and said, "Leave us alone." Now, it is not quite clear. Did he say that to the person who entered the office? Because I understood that the Prosecutor was asking what was Mr. Krnojelac's response to the request of the witness and his brother. So could we have this clarified, whether this sentence was addressed to the guard or, rather, that person who entered or was that addressed to the witness and his brother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Don't --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just wait for a moment. Mr. Bakrac, the question was: "What was Mr. Krnojelac's response?" which is an imprecise word. And the witness was merely telling us what I understood to be his reaction, not what -- his answer or what he had said in answer to the Prosecution's question. May I suggest, leave it to the Prosecution. They'll sort that one out. If they don't feel it's an answer to their question, they can ask again. But there is certainly no ambiguity in the answer. And the fact that it may be a non-responsive answer does not mean that it is not relevant to the case. Now, Mr. Lojo, you wanted to explain your answer, did you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think there will be any logic in his doing so, namely, after that individual entered the office to control it -- to check it from time to time. I don't think there would be any logic in Mr. Krnojelac saying that to us, that is, that he expected an answer from us. He told the individual who entered and he was bothering us in our regular conversation. He told him, "Just leave us alone," and, "Close the door when you leave."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, I'd like to go back to -- sorry. Mr. Lojo, I'd like to go back to Mr. Krnojelac's attitude to your request for release from the KP Dom. What did he say in response to your request?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that as far as he knew, something was being done about an exchange, that is, to have some detainees released through Montenegro. And he even gave us some order of magnitude, that is, a busful, that is, that there was this suggestion, which was under consideration, that a busful of prisoners should leave the prison, that is, and go through Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that you may have been on that bus on the basis of what Mr. Krnojelac said?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not promise anything to me directly, but that is how I understood it. I thought it would be natural, seeing that I was the one who was asking about it, that it would be only logical for me to be on that bus too and to go to Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this meeting was completed, were you ever taken for exchange from the KP Dom before, obviously, you left in 1994?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On another occasion, and I think it was sometime in mid-July, I was taken for some exchange or other, but it never took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this failed exchange, did you ever meet with Mr. Krnojelac again?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was summoned twice because of failed exchange; once by an inspector, whose name was Koprivica; and a few days later, or perhaps ten days later or so, I was also summoned by Krnojelac, together with Rasim Jusufovic. I think -- I don't know if he will be a witness or not. Excuse me, I do not have a list of protected witnesses in front of me; perhaps it would be useful for me to have it. And so we talked; Mr. Krnojelac wanted to know why the exchange had failed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'd better have Exhibit P397, which the witness had on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Mr. Koprivica? You said he was an inspector.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Koprivica, yes, is one of the inspectors who interrogated prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this second meeting held with Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not absolutely sure, but I think it took place in the same place, that is, in structure 2, which I have already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that you were summoned by Mr. Krnojelac. How were you taken to the room in which Mr. Krnojelac was in?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the guards on duty came again with a piece of paper, read out my name, and told me I was to go and see the warden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw Mr. Krnojelac in that room, what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me why did I think the exchange had been thwarted, and I told him what I had heard from guards who had taken us for the exchange; that the reason for it was that the Bosniak side from Gorazde did not want to exchange military captives, prisoners of war, from the front for a mass of civilians. In the group in which I was for the exchange, there was also a group of civilians rounded up from the youth centre or the Partizan Physical Culture Club, and those were mostly women; there were also some 80-year-old men and lots of small children. They were on a separate bus and we were on a truck, on a small truck.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything -- sorry. Was there anything further promised from Mr. Krnojelac after this discussion about the failed exchange or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I mean, I repeated once again, "Well, is there some possibility for us to go out?" I cannot remember it down to the last word, but it could have been in that sense that some information was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anything further discussed at the meeting other than this failed exchange?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course we tried to discuss food whenever we had some opportunity to do so because at that time the quality of food was very poor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Krnojelac's response to that? What did he say in relation to the food?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I believe he mentioned that he would try to see about slightly increasing the quantity of bread, and in about half a month or so, another slice of bread was added to our rations or, rather, half a slice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the food, was anything further discussed?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no. It was a very brief conversation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what functions and responsibilities Mr. Krnojelac had at the KP Dom, from what you observed or from what you heard?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I knew about the post of warden, he had very high authority; he was even closely linked to the republican authorities before. But how things were regulated at that time and what his powers were at that time, I couldn't really say anything about that. These were special times, times of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that Mr. Krnojelac was the warden of KP Dom. What led you to believe that? What was the basis of you concluding that he was the warden of KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier on we had had information from the guards that he was the warden. If anybody was to be spoken to, he was the only person who was competent, who was in charge of dealing with certain requests, wishes, et cetera. Had I not known that he was the warden, I certainly would not have asked for a meeting with him, nor would anything like that have taken place. Sorry. Also, there would not have been any point in him asking me to come and see him and asking why the exchange was not carried through. This only meant that he was a person who did have certain powers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you met Mr. Krnojelac on two occasions, you had two meetings with him. Did you see him at the KP Dom other than those two meetings throughout the weeks that he was present?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him often, especially in the morning when he toured the buildings, especially the kitchen, I guess; perhaps also the other facilities. Perhaps he also went to the furniture factory. Often, I think, he was accompanied by the other officials of the KP Dom, that is to say, his associates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are some of the other officials at the KP Dom that you saw Mr. Krnojelac with? If you don't know, just say "I don't know"; but if you do, if you could state their names.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can certainly remember one name or a few names. I mentioned the commander of the guards, Mitar Rasevic. And I would also mention the deputy, his deputy; that was Todovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Todovic do at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Todovic, I think, in my opinion, was in charge of direct contacts with the prisoners and of the organisation of certain things that had to be done. I think he was also authorised for the allocation of prisoners in different cells. He would also set up working groups for certain things that were to be done. He would also give lists to guards and tell them that certain things had to be done. Of course, he did certain things that I believe he should not have done; I am referring to matters of security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Todovic's first name?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Savo. Savo Todovic. I've just remembered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you think that Mr. Todovic was Mr. Krnojelac's deputy? What led you to believe that? What led you to know that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we got that information from the guards too. If persons were to see the warden, then they would not see Todovic. Todovic behaved like a man who also had high authority, especially high authority in respect of direct contacts with prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Todovic wear at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wore different clothes. Sometimes he wore a camouflage uniform, but a lot of times he wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he wore camouflage, what colour was that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot specify that very accurately. Usually he had a military jacket, green, but most of the time he wore some kind of civilian clothes; or a combination of civilian and military clothes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Mr. Krnojelac wore at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw Krnojelac in civilian clothes, only in a camouflage military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what colour camouflage?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is multi-coloured, green, white.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of whether Mr. Krnojelac had an office at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I directly did not know. I mean, that means that perhaps I was not in his office, but it would have been normal, all things considered, for him to have an office. A warden of a prison has the highest authority there, and it is only natural for him to have an office. And around the office, there should be other auxiliary rooms that are needed for meetings with his collaborators, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do not know where that office was?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where this office was of the previous pre-war warden. It was here in this building number 2, and it was somewhere upstairs. I think it was perhaps on the top floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicates building number 2, top floor, on Exhibit P88.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated that that was the place where the previous warden's office was. Do you know whether that office was used by Mr. Krnojelac or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He's already said that he doesn't know. Is there any point in asking him again?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that what your objection was, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long Mr. Krnojelac was the warden at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know exactly, but I believe for sure it must have been all of 1992 that he was at the KP Dom, perhaps even part of the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of Mr. Krnojelac leaving the KP Dom at some stage?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we knew. During one stage, he had simply disappeared. Instead of him, I assume that all the duties of deputy warden were carried out by Mr. Savo Todovic. As far as I can remember in terms of time, Savo Todovic carried out these duties on his own perhaps for about ten months or so, perhaps even a year, because later, a new warden came again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to ask you some questions about the treatment of Muslim detainees whilst you were at KP Dom. I'd first like to ask you by looking at an exhibit that will be put in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: In fact, the exhibit that is in front of him at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the map on the ELMO. For the year of 1992 and 1993, what room did you stay in?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Room 15, building number 8, on the top floor, to the right from the entrance door. That is Room 15. That is where I spent most of my time. However, first I was brought to this room here. I think that was Room 13. Perhaps this was 11. The shape of the rooms is the same except that they are one underneath the other. I think that in my statement I said that this was Room 13, but it is possible that it might have been 11 as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate Room 15 on that drawing by keeping the pointer still on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: While he's doing that it should be alerted that he's pointing at what we've just been describing as building A. It's not so labelled on this document, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: For me this is number 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It was not a criticism, Mr. Lojo. We have another document where the building is labelled as "A", and the one on the right-hand side [Realtime transcript read in error "left side"] is building B, and it's the other document, I think, that we'll be referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: On the ELMO, Your Honour, I see the figure "A" on the left-hand side of the building. It's small.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It certainly is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicated a room on the section of the building adjoining building A and building B, on the top floor, and the right-hand side window.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Room 15?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think until mid-September. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. I notice in the transcript that if I am correctly reported, I had building A on the right and building B on the left. I don't think I actually said that, but if I did, it should be corrected. The building on the left is building A and the building on the right is building B.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at a photograph from P18. The number is 7472, and it's a picture of two buildings. Can you tell the Court whether or not you're familiar with that view? Mr. Lojo, if you look at the top photo, is that a view that's familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is the view from my room, if I see this right. This view is not directly from my room. This is perhaps from building B. So this view is well familiar to me. This is the entrance or the exit for guards and prisoners. That same exit or entrance is here. It's that door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lojo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: He indicates -- the witness indicates on the photograph at the top of the page, 7472, the door underneath figure 1 as the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And as the view from his room.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The one below, he says, is probably from a room in building B.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you some questions about interviews and interrogations that took place at the KP Dom. Whilst you were in custody in the KP Dom, were you interviewed?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was taken only for a short time to give a statement. I think it was between the 24th and 25th of April, because I was brought on the 19th. I gave a statement at a very early stage. And it was supposed to be signed as well. However, later, I was never taken for any interviews or interrogations. Well, I mean, interviews, conversations, yes, but I was never taken for an interrogation by a police officer, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were interviewed, who were you interviewed by?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was interviewed by Inspector Vladicic. I think his name is Zoran, Zoran Vladicic. Should I say what the contents of this interview was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can briefly state the contents.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a short statement confirming that I was brought to prison, to the KP Dom. Inspector Vladicic asked me only whether I was a member of the SDA, the Party of Democratic Action. He said, "Feel free to say so. It's not important even if you are a member." And I said I was not a member, as I was not. And that's how it all ended. I think that the statement consisted of five to eight lines only. I signed it. In the meantime, yet another one of the inspectors saw me, Petko Gasevic. Since he worked in Maglic, in the laboratory, earlier on, I knew him well. We worked together. He tried to ascertain my status over the telephone. He was doing this in this other room. Judging by the expression on his face, I came to the conclusion that I would not get out of the KP Dom soon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this interview, were you told why, why you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Nobody told me why I was detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other Muslim detainees interviewed at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that your interview commenced on about the 24th or 25th of April. When were the other Muslim detainees --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- when were they interviewed?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other detainees were interviewed for a longer period of time. I think until mid-July. They were being interviewed throughout that period. Unfortunately, they were not interviewed as kindly as I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier that about 700 to 750 Muslim detainees were present in the KP Dom around July 1992. Did you observe or did you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. He said from 650 to 700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That is my memory also, but I haven't got the transcript open. Have you got a different page reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't have the final version of the transcript. It's not an important point. It's just that on my version of the transcript it had been corrected to 700 to 750. Now, maybe this is not the final version, but it's not the main point of the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Maybe you might like to put it at "about 700."

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the amount of Muslim detainees at the KP Dom in July was about 700, 650 to 700. Of those detainees, do you know approximately what percentage of them were interviewed, just from speaking to other prisoners and from your own observations at the time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is very hard to tell what the percentage was of those who had been interviewed. If I were to try to give an estimate in this regard, then I think that since the process of interviews went on all the way up to mid-July, I think about 100 persons were interviewed. I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. could not really say anything more precise than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was doing the interviews at the KP Dom? You've mentioned two men that interviewed -- or one man that interviewed you. Do you know the names of the interviewers, the main ones?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all inspectors carried out interviews. One of their names was already mentioned, Zoran Vladicic. Then there was this Gasevic, Petko Gasevic. There was Koprivica. And there was another one, one more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would detainees be called for interviews? What was the general procedure?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the procedure was the following: The guard who was supposed to take a person out for an interview would come to the room with a small piece of paper with the names of the persons that were being called for an interview. At that time, we were all locked in. He would unlock the room, walk into the room, read out the names, take them out of the room, and take them for an interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what regularity would the interviews occur? Would they occur on a daily basis, a weekly basis? Can you provide some -- do you know how regular these interviews were?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those interviews, the ones that went on until mid-July, took place practically every day. Perhaps only on Saturdays and Sundays there were less because those were not working days, but interviews did take place every day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was selected for interviews? Was there a certain type of detainee selected?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time of course, at least I could not come to see any of the criteria according to which people were chosen; however, later, when things can be analysed and when a definite mosaic is being made, then we can see that the members of the Party for Democratic Action were in the forefront. Then also policemen who were ethnic Muslims were also the first on the line, so to speak. Of course, there were many Muslim detainees, but not all were Muslims. There was a symbolic number of Croats; perhaps three or four of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that some people, some detainees, weren't treated as well as you were when you were interviewed. Do you know of any people that were mistreated during their interviews?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Unfortunately, I know of quite a few people who were mistreated, and I must say that my experience of all these interviews was quite dramatic. I was afraid that I would be called out too. I remember, for instance, Zulfo was in my room; Veiz is his last name. Then there was a Muharem Causevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could just stop there, Mr. Lojo. Can you explain to the Court what you know about Zulfo Veiz's treatment during an interview?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo Veiz. What I know is that in the late afternoon a guard came to fetch him. He expected to be called out, because we had walked up and down the room together and he really was worried. And it turned out that his fears were justified, because in the evening he was called in for interrogation - we could hear it from the room - and he was tortured terribly; he was beaten so that he fainted. They poured water over him, and we could hear calls, "Zulfo, answer. Zulfo, say something." And I think that he was liquidated that evening with another three persons who went for interviews that same evening. I believe they were liquidated because that night I could also hear shots, among other things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zulfo Veiz was in your room, Room 15; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifteen, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear the beating of Zulfo?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, him and others. One could hear it very well because the administrative building is not far from us. Besides, they beat people so forcefully that they also screamed forcefully.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the map which is to your left, can you point to which building you heard the beating coming from on that night?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I think it was from Room 1 -- no, not Room 1, building 1, and perhaps some from building 2; buildings 1 and 2. That is how the sounds reached us, us who were in Room 15. Of course, needless to say, at the exact source of that sound I couldn't really point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness indicates building 1 and 2 on Exhibit P88.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that on that same evening when Zulfo Veiz was beaten, that three others were also taken and beaten as well. Do you know those other three?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some I did know very well; for instance, Kuloglija, him I knew very well because he was a teacher at the elementary, at grade school. And then of course I knew Causevic very well because he was in my room too. But Causevic was not taken out that night, he was summoned for questioning before that. I don't have the list with me of some persons, and such a list would be welcomed by me to jog my memory, to remember some men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that on the night that Zulfo Veiz was taken out and you heard the beatings, that you also heard shots; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I think that that evening four persons -- among other people, four persons were taken away, tortured, battered, and finally - I guess, of course; I didn't see - killed because I could hear four shots.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, the witness is asking for a list. Exhibit P55 is Schedule C with the list, if that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: We can go to the list, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, if you could look at the names on that list and tell the Court if there are any individuals on that list that you knew that were present at KP Dom, and also whether you knew what had happened to them at KP Dom, if anything. If you could start from the top and work your way down. THE COURT REPORTER: Could the list please be put on the ELMO, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 10, Nail Hodzic; 11, Mate Ivancic; 13, Halim Konjo; 15, Mustafa Kuloglija; 17, Krunoslav Marinovic; 19, Nurko Nisic; 25, Kemal Tulek; 26, Enes Uzunovic; 28, 29, brothers Veiz, Veiz brothers, Munib and Zulfo. Other names, yes, I've heard them. I know the names but I didn't know those people so well. For instance, Cankusic, I know there were two sons and a father who were called Cankusic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to refer to the --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, I'd like you only to refer to the individuals on that list that you knew were at KP Dom. Now, you've mentioned a number of names, and you've also mentioned names number 3 and 4. Were they at KP Dom; do you know?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am positive that there were two sons, but whether these are their names, Abdurahman and Refik, I'm not sure; and their father. And I know that they were all in Room 11, in the penitentiary. I know that they were beaten very badly and that it was very hard on the father, because the father could hear his sons screaming as they beat them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Abdurahman Cankusic, can you give us a few details about him? Who was he? How old was he? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I only know their father because he worked at Maglic. He was in the semi-manufactures factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Cankusic, do you have any particulars -- personal particulars that you know of?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith, I should be the last one to be critical of anybody's pronunciation of Yugoslav names, but it would help everybody, particularly the typists, I think, if you gave the number before you referred to the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. You're correct. I should do in short course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the individuals on the list, numbers 3 and 4, Cankusic, that they were in Room 11 and that they were beaten. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from fellow inmates because they saw them being taken downstairs for interrogation and listened to their torture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After those interrogations, are you aware from other prisoners whether or not those people have ever been seen alive again?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, all that I learnt was that these people were among the wanted persons. And I think that this list could be much longer than this, because in the rooms we tried to keep a record, and we listed some 37 persons who had been taken for interrogation, beaten, and had never come back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at individual number 10, Nail Hodzic, what particulars do you know about that person, what personal particulars, briefly?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know quite a great deal about that person. He was a driver, a bus driver, by profession. For awhile he worked at Maglic. I do not know where he then went to work. In the KP Dom, I also know that he had been assigned to drive a vehicle; that he went out at times evidently to perform some jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to Nail Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt -- I do not know what happened to him. What I do know is that he is among the persons being traced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything through other prisoners about what may have happened to Nail Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I did not. I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the individual under number 11, Mate Ivancic.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mate Ivancic, 19 -- no, which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 11.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in your room?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was. Yes, I know him well and I remember him well, because he once extended first aid to me on one occasion. I think that Mate was a nurse; I think that that was his training. I remember how once when I collapsed in the kitchen, when I fainted, he was the one who helped me come to and recover. As a matter of fact, he extended first aid to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of anything happening to --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of anything happening to Mate Ivancic at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if anything happened to him in KP Dom, but as far as I can remember, he was taken for exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you heard of Mate Ivancic being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 13, Halim Konjo, was he at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Konjo. Yes, he was in the penitentiary. I really did not know him much. All I know is that he ran his own coffee shop in the old part of the town. I know he was also taken out and beaten considerably. Otherwise, in this war, people who had money and private capital, they really experienced major tragedies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he was beaten, do you know whether he was returned back inside the KP Dom or not?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think that he was returned, and I believe that he was on that -- those -- on the list of those 37 persons that, as I've told you, we've kept record of at that time who had been taken out and not brought back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of Mr. Konjo being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would like at number 15, Mustafa Kuloglija, was he at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I know him well. I know that he was taken out several times and beaten, thoroughly beaten. And I think he was one of those four whom I mentioned that they had been taken away, beaten, and that at the end of that I had heard some shots and I believe they were intended for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of Mr. Kuloglija being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think he is. I have not heard from anyone that he was alive. I know his wife well, but I did not see her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The individual number 17, Krunoslav Marinovic, was he at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... personal particulars, briefly?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that I know that he had a TV repair shop at the old town market.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him at KP Dom, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened to him. All I know is that he was taken away rather early in the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "taken away early in the day," where was he taken to?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they took him for questioning or for exchange or something. I don't know, but he was taken away from the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that or did you hear that from other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see him being taken away, but it can be confirmed by -- I don't know. The man simply did not turn up again. We, the others, saw each other, but we did not see him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know of Mr. Marinovic being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. From what I heard from my colleagues was that he was also missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the individual 19, Nurko Nisic, was he at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nineteen, you mean. I have him under 19, not under 18. It may have been a slip, the interpreter's slip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 19, Nurko Nisic.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know Nurko Nisic quite well. I know that for a while he worked for the police, the Secretariat of the Interior, and that then he worked for the Assembly. I know that he was taken out several times and beaten. Once at the lunchtime, I know that somebody came and called out his name and took him into the administrative building, and he returned some 10 or 15 minutes later and here he had a huge blue bruise because somebody had slapped him. And I also know that he is one of those who are missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was the blue bruise? What part of his body?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on his left cheek. I think that's where it was. The left cheek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that he was beaten a couple of times. After --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After being beaten on the last time, did you see him again at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of Mr. Nisic being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he's not alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Individual 25, Kemal Tulek, was he at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and beaten very badly, and spent in solitary confinement at least three months. When he came out, he had a beard down to his waist. What happened to him later. Well, later I heard that he was missing, that he's among those whom people are trying to trace. And we related it to the fact that his brother was a professional pilot and must have refused to participate in the war and that that could be one of the reasons for which he enjoyed special treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know when he was beaten?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the early days. And he spent a long time in solitary confinement, I'm telling you, some three months. What happened to him later, that is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever had of Mr. Tulek being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one told me anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Individual number 26, Enes Uzunovic, was he at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is a person who succumbed because his ulcer burst, then, yes, I know that he was there, and I believe that that was him. His ulcer was perforated one day, and it took a long time to get one of the guards to intercede and transfer him to the hospital. We could see how it was very slow and very sloppy. And then we learned that he died on his way to the hospital or in the hospital, if that is the person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And individual number 28, Munib Veiz, was he at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are two brothers, Munib Veiz and Zulfo. Zulfo was in my room throughout and Munib was in 11. I know that from the first day of their detention, both were beaten tremendously. And I -- about Munib, I'm also sure that the last time that he went for questioning, that that same night he was also -- well, either died of injuries or was shot from a pistol or some firearm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the last time that he went for questioning? Do you know what month and year?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo Veiz, do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Munib Veiz.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Munib. I cannot tell you exactly about Munib because he was in a different room, in number 11. And Zulfo Veiz, I'm almost 100 per cent sure it was on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you learn about Munib Veiz being beaten?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because people saw him being taken away for questioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after being taken away to be questioned and beaten, did he return to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not. After the last time he was questioned, but he was questioned on various occasions. He's one of those 37 persons or so who did not come back to the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of Munib Veiz being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the individual 29, Zulfo Veiz, are you aware of him being alive today?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not think he is alive, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your room, Room 15, on about how many occasions did you hear the sounds of beating from the administration building?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose the simplest way to put it is daily or every evening, because questioning and beatings would sometimes take all day, from the morning until 12.00 at night. Sometimes perhaps less. Sometimes only until 10.00 in the evening, but sometimes they would last until 12.00 at night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "daily." Over what period of time are you referring to these daily beatings, a month, two months, or can you state what period of time that was the most intense period?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the most intense period, May, June, until the middle of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sounds could you hear from the building, the administration building, whilst these interrogations were being conducted?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were howls, screams. Of course -- excuse me -- I could, of course, hear the voices of inspectors from time to time, or whoever, trying to obtain some information, and he was trying to get it by beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I believe it's 11.00 on that clock, 10.57 on the transcript, but probably a time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think you'll find that probably every clock in this building is different. We get quite used to it after awhile. All right. We will adjourn now until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, before the break you mentioned the daily beatings that occurred in the administration building and the howls and screams that you heard from that building in your room. I'd like you now to provide a few more details about the day that Zulfo Veiz was taken out of your room. Do you remember what time of the day he was taken out, whether it was during the day or in the evening or late at night?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the evening, on the 13th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the room when he was taken out?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who took him out?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not recall. The duty guard came and took him away, one of the guards who was on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the only person taken out from your room?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think he was, I think he was the only one from our room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take note --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Perhaps the only one in the evening. But during the course of the day, I'm not sure. Perhaps Muharem Causevic was also taken out during the course of the day, but I'm not sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe what happened to Zulfo Veiz after he was taken out of the room? Did you look out of your window, or did you not observe any further?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I looked through the window only for a short period of time, I think, but I did not have the courage to look down or to listen. Usually when people were beaten up, I would put pillows on my ears, on my head, because this had a terrible effect on me. I was terribly frightened. I just couldn't listen to all these screams and cries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he was taken out, did you hear anything from the administration building?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard him being beaten up. Some of the interrogators were saying, "Zulfo," calling out his name, that is, "Zulfo, Zulfo, come to." I think that they were asking him where some weapons were. As far as I could understand from the context, they were looking for weapons. And those were the words that were heard most during these interrogations: "Where are the weapons?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did this beating go on for?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: His beating probably went on for at least two hours. I cannot say for sure, but it must have been at least two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can recall correctly, you said earlier today that shots were also heard on this day.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those shots, were they heard before or after Zulfo Veiz was beaten?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think after the shots, I mean after 2300 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did those shots come from? From within the KP Dom or outside?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside, in the building, because the sound was muffled, that is to say, from the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the shots were heard, did you hear or observe anything else?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Often one could hear engines, motor vehicles being driven away, something thrown onto a vehicle; however, you could not see that because it was on the other side of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "often." But did you hear a vehicle on this particular night, or was it on some other nights?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, that night as well, yes. On several occasions, my colleagues who were more courageous and who spent more time standing by the window, they said that they saw a truck, a vehicle, transporting prisoners towards the bridge, towards the river. And they even heard them being thrown into the river; however, I did not have the courage to listen to all of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn this information about -- this particular day when Zulfo Veiz was taken and beaten, when did you learn this extra information from other prisoners? That night or the following day or at a later time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably on the next day, immediately on the next day, because it was late, around 2300 hours, 2400 hours -- 2300 hours most probably. And some perhaps discussed it immediately. However, very soon people would hear about it. If not that same evening, I would hear about it immediately on the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you heard shots on this particular day at the KP Dom coming from the administration building. Were there any other days that you heard shots coming from the administration building or inside the KP Dom or immediately outside of it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning the situation regarding the detainees, those who were being interrogated and beaten up, I cannot say that I heard shots earlier. However, that night I heard four shots for sure during these late hours, around 2300 hours, between 2300 and 2400 hours; four shots within a short span of time. I then came to the conclusion that four persons were killed, were shot. I did not see this with my very own eyes, but that is the conclusion I came to. As regards shots on other days, the detainees who were with me in the same room said that those -- I mean, those who would watch what was going on more than I did, they said that they would hear shots from outside the KP Dom at a distance from where the current railway bridge is on the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your evidence that the most intensive period for interrogations and interviews was May, June, and July in 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, did you discuss with other prisoners about how many people were taken to be interviewed, interrogated, beaten, and never seen again?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already mentioned earlier that of course we were always in contact. And I said that in my room we had recorded 37 persons who had been taken away, mistreated, beaten up, and probably liquidated, because they never returned to the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say 37 from your -- in your room, are you referring to 37 people that were interrogated, beaten, and taken away from the whole of the KP Dom, from all of the rooms, or are you just referring to 37 people being interrogated, beaten, and never seen again from people that came from your room? Does it relate to your room or the whole of the KP Dom that figure?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That room, of course, does not relate to our room only. It relates to all rooms, approximately, where detainees were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where would you discuss with other prisoners to arrive at and find out about how many people were believed to be taken out in that way? Where would you communicate this information?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rooms. It is in our room that we sort of kept this record. One of the persons who kept pretty good records is a person who will be testifying before this Court as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that person's number appear on the sheet in front of you? If it doesn't, don't mention his name.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, number 86.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to talk about some specific individuals that were taken for interviews and returned, returned to the KP Dom, returned to the rooms after the interview. I would like to ask you about a few individuals that appear in your statements, and the first person I would like to ask is Halim Dedovic. Do you know him? Was he at KP Dom, and what do you know happened to him, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Halim Dedovic was in the same room with me for quite some time. It is not Room 15. At that time, I was together with him in Room 18. Halim Dedovic was a barber. He was very busy giving people shaves and haircuts, not only amongst us but also among the officials. Later on, among the Serb prisoners as well. As far as his fate is concerned, all I know is that this person has not been heard from. And I've always wondered why this man, who did so many services to both sides, why was he killed too? According to some criteria or the other. Of course, all of it is strange, but I know that he gave the higher officials and the guards haircuts, as well as prisoners of Serb ethnicity. He was taken out for some kind of exchange, and his fate is unknown or, rather, he is still missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how he was treated at the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He personally told me that when he was brought to the KP Dom, he recognised a guard called Burilo. As people were brought in -- this man is very strong, very corpulent. I think that he weighs about 120 to 130 kilogrammes. As soon as he would hit someone with his baton, they would pass out. That's what Dedovic said to me. "He hit me and I did not fall." Then he was surprised and he said, "Wow, look at him. He didn't even fall," and then he hit him again until he fell. That's what he told me, and that has to do with the way in which he was brought into custody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was he brought into custody? Do you know or did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he told me. I think that he was probably among the first to be brought into custody. He was brought in from the garden, from his own garden. He wanted to do something in the garden, and the Chetniks came and one of them said, "I know that you are not to be blamed for anything, but you're a Muslim and we have to take you in," and that's how they took him in. I know him well because I played chess with him very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to refer to Avdo Mehmedspahic. Do you know him? Was he at KP Dom, and do you know anything that happened to him there?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Avdo Mehmedspahic was also in the KP Dom. I'm not sure exactly which room he was in. I know that he was beaten up terribly. I know that he was so beaten up that he could not stand on his feet. On one occasion, I saw him when I was going out for an interview with one of the inspectors. He could not walk up stairs. I had to hold him and help him. He was shaking something terrible. I had never seen a person shake or tremble that way in all my life. Perhaps he was very frightened of being beaten up that badly again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is also among the persons who are still missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see him in that beaten-up state?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That must have been in the first half of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what type of -- were there any obvious injuries on him, to you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see. He was dressed, of course, and he also had some kind of footwear on his feet, some light footwear, but could I see that he could not stand on his feet because of all the pain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he from your room?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say to you who caused him to be beaten up, who beat him up?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not in a position to ask him. I encountered him only at the staircase at the entrance in the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know an Asim Mezbur. Was he at the KP Dom, and do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mezbur. Yes. He was in my room, number 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him, if anything, at the KP Dom, in terms of treatment? Was he well treated?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was not treated well. I think that he was beaten up badly before he was brought to the KP Dom; however, during his stay in my room, he was not taken out for beatings. He only went off on an exchange. That exchange was, I think, sometime in the beginning of September, or perhaps even earlier. Perhaps earlier. I can't say for sure now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Suko Misic, was he at KP Dom? And do you know if anything happened to him there in terms of bad treatment?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood the name and surname correctly, that is number 19 on the list, 55, Nisic, Nurko --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can stop you there, Mr. Lojo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, it must be my pronunciation again. The person I'm referring to is Suko Misic; S-u-k-o, surname Misic, M-i-s-i-c. And he doesn't appear on any lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You can understand the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a Suko Misic from the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think the name should be Zuko with a "Z". I will like to see the name and surname written out. On the list, I have a name that is Nisic, Nurko, and you say that that is not it. I don't know of any Zuko Nisic. I haven't got any information about such a person, and I think that I did not mention such a person in my statement either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last individual I'd like you to think about is Nurija Rahman. Was he at the KP Dom? And do you know of anything that happened to him?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was in my room; I think that at that time we were in Room 14. One day, together with some other detainees, he went out to pick some plants that we used to prepare tea, some herbs; and sometimes we would also put this into our food and mix it together. On that occasion, somebody from the administrative building noticed him, called the guard, and the guard took him to a solitary cell. And in front of the solitary confinement cell, he hit him on the head so badly - he was a very thin person; I think that he weighed less than 50 kilos - that he passed out. I know that we had to try to bring him to in the room. He also got a catheter; he couldn't go to the toilet. Actually, he was paralysed after that, his left arm or right leg. I can't remember now. We had to carry him. And we managed to help him recuperate. Later he could stand on his own two feet, and he managed to heal. He was exchanged together with us on the 6th of October, 1994, when this main group was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this beating occur?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say. I think it was 1993, I think it was sometime in mid-1993. I know that it was the guard named Pljevaljcic who hit him. As for the others who were with him, he beat them up; they were beaten up by a guard named Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you that it was this guard that beat him up?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw them being taken through the building. We saw these guards taking them through the building. Rahman himself told us who had hit him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your room, Room 15, did you see Muslim detainees being brought into the KP Dom for the first time, on their arrival?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any instances of bad treatment of these detainees as they arrived?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very often they were thrown into the compound as they were being beaten, through the door that I showed you on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many times did you see this occur?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
