"When Krnojelac left his post, he was replaced by his hitherto deputy Savo Todovic, and his authority was extensive. Todovic behaved as if he had full authority over military and security matters. He would call out people's names and check on people at all times of the day. He would personally interrogate people, beat them, and put them into solitary confinement. I never heard that Krnojelac had used his authority to abuse people in this way. On the other hand, I don't know what authority Krnojelac had to prevent abuse." The text continues about Todovic being warden then, and we already heard about that from this witness. I would like to ask the witness whether he did say this, whether this is his statement, whether he signed it and whether he read it when he gave this statement to the investigator of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I point out that I said "as if," "as if." He behaved "as if."

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said "as if," it means that he may not necessarily have had that kind of --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was my only question.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, I fully abide by this statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you talked about punishment that was meted out upon detainees, you said that the reason for this were trifles and attempts to escape. What about these trifles? Are you referring to infractions in terms of prison discipline?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that on one occasion you saw new detainees being brought in and that the guards were beating them as they were entering the compound. Could you tell us exactly where this happened and where you were, in which room?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there was a good view from my room, Room 15, of the entrance gate. Exit gate too, but let's call it the entrance gate. When detainees were being brought in, they were roughly thrown into the compound and very often they were beaten as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell me whether they beat them within the compound?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Within the compound, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you say to the investigator of the OTP, on the 19th and 20th of November, 1995, that you had heard that a lot of Muslims had been killed on their way to the KP Dom and that the members of their families believed that they were in the KP Dom and that was actually not the case?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You talked about a prisoner who died, unfortunately, because he could not take food since he had a problem with his mouth. Do you know what kind of a problem this was that he had with his mouth?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know exactly because I was not in his room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you only heard about it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about it because we were in contact amongst ourselves, and I heard that he had this problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you hear this from? Can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody from that Room 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the name?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you a few names now of persons from that room if that means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think it would mean something to the Defence, because they are the only persons whom we can ask about the problems that this detainee had.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted). Then there was --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm afraid to mention names now because they might be witness names. I have only three names here, I mean, with numbers, so I don't know. Perhaps I will be mentioning a protected name. I don't know, and I do apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that your problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: That is my concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Of course, if he mentions a name and somebody later on is called as a witness, nobody is going to tie the two together if that witness has got protective measures. But have you got a list of the witnesses that you can give Mr. Lojo?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have produced a list, but we have only put on is list the names that we expected he would say. Therefore, I have no list at the moment to give to him except for the entire witness list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But the point that I was making was that if he mentions names, all we know is that they are detainees in the prison. We don't know that they're going to give evidence. If they do give evidence later and if they do have protective measures, there is no way in which somebody else can tie the two together, surely.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So you proceed, Mr. Lojo.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one of them was a witness recently and that's why I paused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Perhaps you better put that name down on a piece of paper and it can be shown to the Prosecution. Then we'll know whether or not it is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, give me a piece of paper, please. I haven't got a pencil or a piece of paper. I wrote the names of three persons. Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, also the name that the witness did give, is that one that should be redacted?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The first name is actually the name he mentioned, and it's actually the Witness 71, I think. Either 71 or 76.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well then, we'll have that one redacted. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The next person he has written down is the Witness 139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So can you put the numbers beside it so he can have the list back?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the third one is not a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we hear the name of the third person who is not -- who will not be testifying?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm asking if we know the two of them are witnesses and both protected witnesses, then how do we go about this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You use the numbers that are beside the two where the numbers have been written, and you may use the name of the third one.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. So I will say person 71 and person 139.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the name of the third person, I've already -- if Mr. Lojo would give us the name of the third person.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather not say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Vasic, if the witness has some problem about revealing his name, we perhaps could give you a look at the document so that you know the name and it need not be stated in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing against that. Thank you very much, Your Honour. Yes, of course I agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And the identity of that witness should not be revealed by you to any person other than your client, of course. If you use the person's -- if you want to use the person's name, you'll have to refer to it by some other pseudonym. Mr. Lojo, have you got any problem with counsel for the accused seeing that name? It won't be made public though. It will be exactly -- it will put him in exactly the same situation as the other two names you have in your list. Counsel for the accused know the identity of those witnesses, but they're not allowed to use their names or to reveal their names or their identity to the public.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was about to -- they're the only ones that I'd really rather not show it or say it. Had I wanted this name to be mentioned among people who have something to do with this case, then I -- and I do not really see why you insist on this at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, at the present time, I would not be disposed to order him to provide it to you. If you've got two names and you want to make some further inquiries, you know who they are, you can proceed. If you have some problem, you come back to us. But the document itself should be marked for identification. It will be marked 2 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. Your Honours, excuse me. May I have your leave? These two persons are witnesses. One has already testified. We have no means of checking except with the witness who is mentioned here, and yet it's not a witness for the Prosecution. The only way we can check what the witness is saying today is to check with that particular person. The other two witnesses for the Prosecution or, rather, the witness for the Prosecution and one of them has already testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The one thing that is clear is that the Prosecution has no ownership of these witnesses. If you want to interview them, you are entitled to do so. So you should not feel in any way reticent about proceeding to talk to the Prosecution's witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understand well, these numbers and this name will be filed and will be kept in the file, won't they? The Defence will try first to ask the witness, the witness for the Prosecution who has not testified yet. So when his turn comes, we shall try to ask him about this individual who had trouble with taking food. And if we do not get the info -- necessary information, then we shall request or apply to the Court to allow that the third name be divulged to us so that we ascertain what happened to that man and how did he die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I should set one thing straight though. It will not be filed. The document will be marked for identification. It will given to the Prosecution to keep because it is their witness. No doubt the Prosecution will speak to Mr. Lojo later to find out the basis of his objection to anybody else seeing that name and it's a matter we can come back to if we have to later on, but it is not an exhibit and it does not go on the official court file.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can even now help. The third person is a very close relative to the witness, and I think this is probably the reason that he doesn't want to say the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that may be so, but you can check up with that later and that would be a very strong reason for not revealing it. But at this stage, we don't have to rule upon it, and Defence counsel have every right to speak to the Prosecution's witnesses of whom some identification has been given by reference to the number, and they know their identity. You can proceed, Mr. Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My question to the witness is related to the KP Dom, that is, is the witness aware that in front of the penitentiary is a road and does he know where that road leads to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It leads to the hospital. To the right to the hospital and to the left into the heart of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it pass in front of the entrance gate into the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about 15 metres or so away from the entrance gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified today about a photograph in Exhibit 18, which is a photograph, 7472, which you were shown by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please help me with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you testified about this photograph, you said that in point of fact, that was a view from the room that you were kept in. The upper photograph, 7472.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this may not be directly the view from my room, but at any rate, something that you can see from Room 15. The room is probably slightly more to the left. But I see no reason for this question. I don't see the purpose of this question. I don't see the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be asked not to pass judgements on questions. The Defence knows why it asks questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I was going to say much the same thing, but you've said it now. Mr. Lojo, you just answer the questions. If there is an objection to be taken to it, it's up to the Prosecution to take the objection. It is a fair enough question. It may be repetitious, that's all.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you, but I don't know. It's not mine to judge the quality of the Defence, but it seems to me I haven't really heard a single right question from the Defence. But, of course, I'm not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence does not wish to comment on this. Your Honour, I'd like to ask the witness which -- in which wing of the KP Dom is Room 15?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it will be best if I show it to you on the other photograph, on that drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness tell us if it's in wing A or wing B?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's neither wing A or wing B. I saw it on that drawing, and I know which are the -- but Room 15 is between wings A and B.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is enough. This view, that we see on the upper photograph, or, rather, the entrance here, one can see it very well here, a very clear view of it, and my question is if you can tell us in which rooms was he kept in and at what periods of time. Because in this statement that he made to the Prosecution, presumably by a slip of the tongue or because that was the testimony, Room 12 is also mentioned, and today we heard from the witness that he was not in that room. So could the witness tell us which rooms was he in and at what times?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is not for you to comment either, Mr. Vasic. If that's the basis of your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you don't want the witness to comment upon your questions, you shouldn't comment upon his answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, you want him to tell you again which rooms he was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In which rooms he was in and the times, from the beginning to the end of his detention, if he could tell us that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I get the drawing of the KP Dom, or is it perhaps somewhere here? It's easier for me. Perhaps it will be easier, it would be best, if I can show it straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There is both that perspective drawing, which has been shown to the witness, and, if I may say so, the more useful document which has the plan layout with the rooms on each floor, which is Exhibit 6/1, from memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just interject here. This witness seems to have more familiarity with the three-dimensional drawings, and the 6/ drawings. They relate to particular levels of the Muslim detention centre, wings A and B. So perhaps it might be more useful to look at the 3-D drawing first and then go from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But when he has been pointing with the pointer there, he's had to point behind a wing that comes out so that we can't really see. If I may suggest, 6/1 is not all that difficult to follow for somebody who sees it for the first time. It has each room with a number on it, and each floor is indicated. Now, surely if we could have that, we will all know what he's talking about rather than having to guess from where he's placing a pointer, half a sentence of the translation from when we're following it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: That may well assist more, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only the ground plan, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. Just wait a moment. This should be all of them. Hasn't he been given all of them? Give him the whole of 6/1, /2, /3, /4, and /5.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, on this drawing, we have the ground floor, the positions of building 1, the storage room; building 2, as it says here. And this is this part which juts out with rooms. Room 15 is in building number 1, in this building here, on the top floor, roughly in this part here. And you wanted to know which rooms I was in?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we cannot see that. We can see that only on the three-dimensional drawing. The ground plans of the rooms are practically identical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but on them you have numbers of rooms.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have no reason for showing the ground plans because it's much more useful to show the movement on a three-dimensional drawing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. If he wants to use the three-dimensional one, then let him use it. But so far as I'm concerned, if he has to point behind a wall, it is very difficult to see. So if he could perhaps have the other -- the plan drawings as well and work, first of all, from the perspective drawing and then from the plans so that we can all follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There might be a simpler solution, Your Honour. I'd ask the witness to give us first the numbers of rooms that he was in; then perhaps it will be easier for us to locate them.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't mind. I was brought to Room 13; that could also be Room 11 because they're one above the other. And when I was brought there, of course, I knew nothing about the KP Dom or the distribution of rooms, so it is very likely that I confused Room 11 and Room 13. From that room I was moved to Room 15, two or three days later; that is, I was brought to that room on the 19th of April, and three or four days I was moved to Room 15. In Room 15 I spent quite a long time, I should say, until the end of July, roughly, that is, end of August and first half of September. And after these major exchanges, because there were a lot of vacancies, a lot of empty rooms, I was moved to Room 18. I think that I was once again, for a short while, I was taken to Room 21 for two, three, maybe four days, and then taken back to Room 18. From Room 18 I then got to Room 14, which is below Room 15, and from Room 14 I was moved to the workers' room, number 13, where I stayed until the end of my detention. I often moved from one room to another. I mentioned that I stayed in some only a short while, and it is possible that I was in yet another room, or perhaps it just seemed to me that I'd been there. But be that as it may, these were the rooms that I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we might save time. The witness need not show us all those rooms because we can easily find them on the ground plans that we have with us. So with your leave, I should like to move on to my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified today that the work group began to work in the Miljevina mine sometime in April/May 1993. Are you sure that it was prior to September 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not -- I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I have just one more question for the witness and it concerns Milorad Krnojelac's house. Do you know where Milorad Krnojelac's house is?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where is it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the area which was called Aladza. I don't know what it's called now, but it is somewhere there. I could not really pinpoint the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that his house was set on fire, and when?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was in the early days and that it was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "early days," you mean the early days of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I guess so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence has no more questions. I should like to thank the witness. And we also wish to tender the exhibit marked ID 171 and its version in B/C/S, 171A. We would like to tender them as Exhibit D2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But, Mr. Vasic, you have got from the witness his acceptance that the passage you read out to him was said to him by the OTP Prosecutor. Why do we need the document? We went through this the other day with the previous witness. We don't want documents just for the sake of having documents. If there had been any dispute that he said it, obviously the statement would have to go in. Do you really need it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence wanted to tender it because of one word, "a soldier in uniform who interrupted." The question was whether he repeatedly interrupted them or not. So it was that one word. But I believe you're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I may be wrong, but I don't recall you putting to the witness that there was an inconsistency between what he said in his statement about that and what he said in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, there was no -- there were no inconsistencies between the statement and the testimony. I asked him about that military policeman who came in - I believe it's clear from the transcript - and the answer was that it wasn't said all that categorically as the question implied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm still not clear. Are you saying now you do not need the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we shall not need that document. We withdraw our suggestion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Any re-examination, Mr. Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Just two questions, thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Smith:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Lojo, you said that you moved out of Room 15 in August or September, you think, at the end of August or September. Are you referring to 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Room 17? Did I hear it well? Or do you mean Room 15?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Room 15.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I left that room and went to Room 18 sometime in the middle of September. Not before that, at any rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which year are you referring to, 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD LOJO [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1992, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question here. I have this document and I believe it belongs to the Prosecution, regarding protective witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that the document on which you wrote the names, Mr. Lojo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you would hand that to the Prosecution as you leave. You may leave now. Thank you for giving evidence. Now, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, the next witness requires protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and it's image alteration and pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. So the blinds have to be brought down to bring him in. I think we'll start tomorrow morning. We'll adjourn now until 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of November, 2000, at 9.30 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.00 p.m.,
